segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yeah, so for HarborPoint tomorrow, I want to keep it tight: invoice approval routing, the manager dashboard, and then the seat true-up question. They said they’re at 68 users now, likely 75 by June.

segments.speaker: Colin
segments.text: Got it. Are they still asking for the two-level approval path, or did finance back off that?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Two-level for anything over $2,500, one-level below that. Pretty standard. I put a sample workflow together with their cost centers, just Sales, Ops, and Field Service.

segments.speaker: Colin
segments.text: Okay. I can show that in about twelve minutes. On pricing, are you holding at the 75-seat tier?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yeah, pricing sheet comes out cleaner that way. $18,900 annual subscription, $4,200 onboarding, net 30. If they push on onboarding I can split it across the first two invoices.

segments.speaker: Colin
segments.text: Makes sense. Small wrinkle, their current workspace says access through April 30, and that’s tomorrow, so if the link acts strange in the session I’ll use my demo environment instead.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Okay, good call. Don’t let us get stuck on permissions. They care more about the approval emails looking readable on mobile.

segments.speaker: Colin
segments.text: Yep. Do they need the billing export in the first go-live, or can that wait?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: They want it by May 20 if possible, but I told them go-live on May 13 is just core routing and reporting. Export can be phase two as long as invoices aren’t manual for more than one cycle.

segments.speaker: Colin
segments.text: Cool. I’ll keep the demo focused and leave five minutes for contract term questions at the end.
